"We’ll Blush To Tell Our Grandchildren" – Great Comment on the Closing of the San Francisco Club

From the San Francisco Chronicle

May 27, 1998

Excerpt from Column by Scott Ostler

THE NEWS is more interesting when you read it very carefully.

Careful reader Dan Machak points out a paragraph in yesterday's Chron story on the shut-down of Dennis Peron's pot club by S.F. Sheriff Michael Hennessey.

The quote is from Eileen Hirst, Hennessey's chief of staff.

``There wasn't very much marijuana -- maybe two big handfuls,'' Hirst said. She said it took 30 to 35 people until noon to finish the inventory.

Followed, no doubt, by a giggle-filled, two-hour lunch break across the street at the donut shop.

Easy prediction: Someday the closing of the med-pot clubs by the feds will be looked upon with at least a tiny bit of the type of wonderment and shame we feel now when we see old photos of ``Colored'' drinking fountains.

©1998 San Francisco Chronicle  Page A3

(Ed. note: Most southerners my age can remember water fountains with the little signs at just above the eye level of a small child. This is very good analogy. How do you explain hatred to a child? We are very good at teaching them to hate, but not very good at explaining it.)
